influenza: Paracetamol for fever and body ache
common_cold: Honey and ginger for the throat
covid19: Pulse oximeter to track oxygen at home
Isolate from others in the household
dengue: Never take ibuprofen or aspirin; they raise bleeding risk
ORS, coconut water and papaya leaf juice as tolerated
Daily platelet monitoring as advised by a doctor
typhoid: Antibiotics are essential but must be prescribed after a blood test
Do not self-medicate with leftover antibiotics
malaria: Antimalarial drugs must be prescribed after a blood smear or rapid test
migraine: Paracetamol or ibuprofen taken early in the attack
Rest in a dark, quiet room
Caffeine in small amounts can help some people
Prescription triptans need a doctor's assessment
tension_headache: Warm compress on the neck and shoulders
Correct screen height and take regular breaks
Avoid painkillers on more than 10 days a month
allergic_rhinitis: Non-drowsy antihistamine such as cetirizine or loratadine
Steroid nasal spray if advised by a doctor
asthma: Use the prescribed reliever inhaler as directed
Never stop a preventer inhaler on your own
Keep a spacer for effective delivery
Seek urgent care if the reliever is not working
bronchitis: Antibiotics rarely help; most cases are viral
pneumonia: Antibiotics are usually required and must be prescribed
Do not manage this at home without an in-person examination
sinusitis: Short course of decongestant spray for no more than 3 days
pharyngitis: A throat swab decides whether antibiotics are needed
gerd: Antacid gel or tablets after meals
Avoid lying down for 3 hours after eating
Raise the head of the bed
Reduce spicy, fried and fatty foods
peptic_ulcer: Avoid NSAID painkillers such as ibuprofen
Testing for H. pylori is usually required
urinary_tract_infection: Drink 2 to 3 litres of water daily
Antibiotics are needed and require a urine test
anemia: Iron supplement taken with vitamin C
Avoid tea or coffee within an hour of iron tablets
Folic acid and B12 if deficient
A blood test is needed to confirm the type
hypertension: Reduce salt to under 5 g a day
Prescription medication is decided by a doctor
diabetes: Get a fasting blood sugar and HbA1c test
Start a controlled diet and daily walking
All diabetes medication must be prescribed
hypothyroidism: A TSH blood test confirms the diagnosis
Thyroid hormone replacement is prescribed and taken on an empty stomach
food_poisoning: Plain rice, banana and toast once vomiting settles
Avoid dairy and oily food for 2 days
conjunctivitis: Clean the eye with cooled boiled water and clean cotton
Do not share towels or pillows
Antibiotic drops only if a doctor advises
arthritis: Paracetamol as first choice for pain
Warm compress for stiffness, cold for swelling
anxiety: Talking therapy is the first-line treatment
chickenpox: Keep nails short to avoid scarring
vertigo: Move the head slowly, especially when getting up
Sit down immediately when an episode starts
Prescribed repositioning exercises help most cases
Anti-vertigo medication needs a doctor's advice
